Series, parallel and feedback connections

Source: R/interconnections.R
ctrl_series.Rd

  • ctrl_series(sys1, sys2): the output of sys1 drives sys2, so the overall transfer function is \(G_2 G_1\) (note the order). The operator form is sys2 * sys1.

  • ctrl_parallel(sys1, sys2): \(G_1 + G_2\) (same inputs, summed outputs); operator form sys1 + sys2.

  • ctrl_feedback(sys1, sys2, sign = -1): closes the loop \(u_1 = r + \mathrm{sign} \cdot y_2\), \(u_2 = y_1\), with output \(y_1\). The default sign = -1 is negative feedback, giving \((I + G_1 G_2)^{-1} G_1\).

  • ctrl_append(...): block-diagonal (parallel, unconnected) stacking.

Usage

ctrl_series(sys1, sys2)

ctrl_parallel(sys1, sys2)

ctrl_feedback(sys1, sys2 = 1, sign = -1)

ctrl_append(...)

Arguments

sys1, sys2

Models or numeric gains.

sign

Feedback sign, -1 (negative) or +1 (positive).

...

Models to append.

Value

A model.

Details

When both models have direct feedthrough the feedback loop contains an algebraic loop; it is resolved by solving with \(I - \mathrm{sign}\, D_1 D_2\), and an error is raised when this matrix is singular or ill-conditioned (the interconnection is then not well posed).

Models must share the time domain; a static gain adopts the time domain of the other model. SISO transfer functions are combined with polynomial arithmetic (without cancellation); all other combinations are carried out in state space.

Examples

G <- ctrl_tf(1, c(1, 1))
C <- ctrl_tf(c(2, 1), c(1, 0))
L <- ctrl_series(C, G)        # G * C
T <- ctrl_feedback(L, 1)      # unity negative feedback
ctrl_poles(T)
#> [1] -0.381966+0i -2.618034+0i
